what: User correction (2026-04-26) on aide_import framing: do NOT call it a hard "anti-pattern" that violates memory #335. The tool has legitimate use cases — (1) one-time seed from a legacy doc that's being DELETED (doc goes away, memory is new home, not a duplicate); (2) external material not in repo docs (Notion, ADR templates, ChatGPT output snippets); (3) import-then-curate (bring in raw, prune to essentials). The anti-pattern is REPEATED import of a maintained repo doc — that's where duplication + drift kicks in. Calibrate framing: aide_import is not "broken vs principle #335"; it's "needs sharpened docstring on appropriate use." Specific recommendation: option 1 (sharpen docs) for 0.5.1, option 2 (idempotency on (what, layer, scope)) if real-world usage shows repeated re-import as dominant.
why: User pushed back on my too-strong "anti-pattern" framing during Cursor validation walk. Important durable correction — when I assess a feature against a principle, I should look at the FULL space of legitimate use cases before declaring it anti-pattern. aide_import has real workflows (legacy migration, external material, raw-then-curate) that are NOT duplication. Anti-pattern framing only fits ONE specific misuse (repeated re-import of live docs). Storing this so future framing of similar tools/features starts more nuanced rather than reaching for "deprecate" prematurely.
